note.text:
To solve a logarithmic equation, change it to index form, or combine the logs into one first.
• log₂ x = 5 → x = 2⁵ = 32.
• log_x 81 = 4 → x⁴ = 81 → x = 3.
• log x + log 4 = log 20 → log 4x = log 20 → 4x = 20 → x = 5.
• log₂ (x − 3) = 4 → x − 3 = 16 → x = 19.
Check every answer: you cannot take the log of zero or of a negative number, so reject such solutions.

sections.heading: Index form
sections.text:
Every log statement is an index statement in disguise: log_b x = n means x = bⁿ.
So log₂ x = {5} gives x = {pw(2, 5)} = {32}, and logₓ {49} = {2} gives x² = {49}, so x = {7} (a base must be positive).
When the unknown is inside a bracket, log₃ (x + {1}) = {2} gives x + {1} = {9}, so x = {8}.

sections.heading: Combining logs
sections.text:
If there are several logs, use the laws to make one log on each side:
log x + log {4} = log {20} → log ({4}x) = log {20} → {mono(4, 'x')} = {20} → x = {5}.
When both sides are a single log of the same base, the insides must be equal.

sections.heading: Checking answers
sections.text:
Logs exist only for positive numbers. In log₂ x + log₂ (x − {2}) = log₂ {15}, you get x(x − {2}) = {15}, so x = {5} or x = {-3}.
x = {-3} would need log₂ ({-3}), which does not exist, so the only solution is x = {5}.
Always substitute back to check.
